The journey to a usable product

Each milestone is something a user can do. Dates are the team’s forecast; if one slips, the date moves and the scope is not cut.

1Try on laptop

Install a single package, run a gated agent on the simulator in under 10 minutes; no hardware, account, or API key needed

Product entry point: anyone can try without spending money on hardware

In progressNov 15, 202696% doneTeam and internal testers

2Physical device on Raspberry Pi

Wire a kit (light, door, fan, sensors, camera, motor) to Pi 5; same agent, same gate as on laptop; connect third-party products (Muse, Home Assistant, existing MCP servers) via plugins and proxies

First time an AI command touches physical hardware while passing through contracts — even commands from other ecosystems

In progressDec 27, 202673% doneTeam, internal testers, and one partner team (proxy portion, neuroedge.guard, sim — Q-70)

3Gate running on a $5 chip

Flash agent to ESP32-S3 (Box-3, M5Stack CoreS3); gate decides directly on chip, blocking correctly even when offline

Safety without cloud dependence; same contract from laptop to microcontroller

In progressafter Assemble and run via conversation, share Blueprints22% doneTeam and internal testers

4Assemble and run via conversation, share Blueprints

Describe device in words to current AI (Claude Code, Claude Desktop); AI writes actions, gates, envelopes, and mission contracts via NeuroEdge MCP tools; NeuroEdge grades, human approves before locking; operator agent monitors device all day, proactively reporting and requesting approval via Telegram; package device into NeuroEdge Blueprint for others to install with a single command

Shrinks building a contracted device from a day to minutes; contracts and traces serve as proof for strangers to install and makers to sell (Q-72) — early milestone, measured by 8-week demand gate

In progressNov 25, 20260% doneTeam, internal testers, and external testers trying Blueprints on simulation via direct hand-off wheel (Q-72)

5Public launch

Anyone can pip install neuroedge; invoke devices from Claude, Home Assistant, or agent frameworks via authenticated MCP

First time external users can use it

In progressLaunchafter Assemble and run via conversation, share Blueprints64% doneEveryone (free non-commercial)

6v1.0 — into production

Signed firmware updates, lock device, 24-hour stable run; meets PRD §11.1 acceptance criteria

Reliable enough for product teams to ship in commercial devices

In progressLaunchafter Assemble and run via conversation, share Blueprints33% doneEveryone; enterprises via commercial license
After v1.0 — 2 milestones: Developer Beta · One chat box for multiple devices, multiple homes

7Developer Beta

50–100 external developers use it for real on the 1.0.x line

Real metrics determine commercial direction (branch point §5.6)

Not startedafter Assemble and run via conversation, share Blueprints0% doneInvited developers

8One chat box for multiple devices, multiple homes

Chat with a single brain monitoring the entire mesh: multiple ESP32s, multiple Pis, multiple homes, multiple roles; self-hosted or NeuroEdge Cloud (Q-74, Q-76)

Cloud subscription provides recurring revenue (conditional, after 8-week gate); cloud coordinates without supreme authority — each node enforces its own rules
